questions.question: Under the Viksit Bharat–G RAM G Act 2025, how many days of statutory wage employment are guaranteed per rural household per financial year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**125 days**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Viksit Bharat–G RAM G Act 2025** is a significant legislative framework designed to enhance rural livelihood by guaranteeing **125 days** of **statutory wage employment** per **financial year** to every **rural household**.
 
• The primary objective of this act is to provide a robust **social security** net for families residing in **rural areas**, ensuring that at least one member of the household can find work when needed.
 
• This guarantee applies to all **adult members** of a **rural household** who volunteer to perform **unskilled manual work**.
 
• Under the provisions of the act, the **125 days** of work is a **legal entitlement**, representing an increase from the previously standard **100 days** offered under earlier schemes like **MGNREGA**.
 
• The act emphasizes **inclusive growth**, specifically targeting **vulnerable groups**, including **Scheduled Castes (SC)**, **Scheduled Tribes (ST)**, and **women**, to ensure they have access to **minimum income** through labor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vision of Viksit Bharat 2047:**
 
 
• The **Viksit Bharat–G RAM G Act 2025** is a foundational step toward the **Viksit Bharat 2047** vision, which aims to transform **India** into a **developed nation** by the **100th year** of its **independence**.
 
• By increasing the **employment days** to **125**, the government aims to reduce **rural-to-urban migration** and strengthen the **rural economy**.
 
 
 
• **Financial Provisions and Wages:**
 
 
• Wages under this act are revised annually and are linked to the **Consumer Price Index-Agricultural Labourers (CPI-AL)** to protect workers against **inflation**.
 
• The **Central Government** typically bears **100%** of the **wage cost** for **unskilled manual labor**, while **material costs** are shared between the **Centre** and the **States** in a **75:25 ratio**.
 
 
 
• **Types of Work Permitted:**
 
 
• The act focuses on the creation of **durable assets** such as **water conservation structures**, **check dams**, **rural roads**, and **afforestation** projects.
 
• Work is also directed toward **natural resource management** and **individual assets** for **small and marginal farmers** to improve **agricultural productivity**.
 
 
 
• **Digital Implementation:**
 
 
• The scheme utilizes the **G RAM G portal** for **real-time monitoring**, **e-attendance** via the **National Mobile Monitoring System (NMMS)**, and **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** to ensure transparency.
 
• **Aadhaar-Based Payment Systems (ABPS)** are mandatory to ensure that the **wages** reach the correct **bank accounts** of the **beneficiaries** without **leakage**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Unemployment Allowance:** If the **government** fails to provide **employment** within **15 days** of the **application for work**, the applicant is legally entitled to a daily **unemployment allowance**.
 
• **Social Audit:** To maintain **accountability**, the **Gram Sabha** is empowered to conduct **social audits** of all the **projects** executed under the **Act** in the **Gram Panchayat**.
 
• **Workplace Facilities:** The act mandates that **facilities** such as **drinking water**, **shade** for periods of rest, and **first-aid boxes** must be provided at every **worksite**.
 
• **Role of Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs):** The **Gram Panchayats** are responsible for **planning** and **implementing** at least **50%** of the works in terms of **cost**, ensuring **decentralized governance**.

questions.question: According to the Economic Survey released in January 2025, India was identified as the seventh most vulnerable country to climate change. What percentage of days in 2024 were marked by significant climate events such as heatwaves, cyclones and floods?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**93%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Economic Survey 2024-25**, which was released in **January 2025**, provides a comprehensive analysis of the Indian economy and highlights the significant challenges posed by environmental factors.
 
• According to the survey, **India** has been identified as the **seventh** most vulnerable country globally to the impacts of **climate change**.
 
• The report startlingly revealed that extreme weather events occurred on **93%** of the days in the calendar year **2024**. This indicates that out of **366 days** (2024 being a leap year), at least one region in India experienced a significant climate event on approximately **340 days**.
 
• These climate events primarily included record-breaking **heatwaves**, devastating **floods**, **landslides**, and intense **cyclones**, reflecting the increasing frequency and intensity of weather anomalies.
 
• The data underscores that climate change is no longer a future projection but a present reality affecting the **geographical** and **economic** stability of the nation.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is 93%.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Impact on Agriculture and Economy**:
 
 
• The **Economic Survey** notes that such frequent extreme weather events have a direct negative impact on **agricultural productivity** and **food security**.
 
• Fluctuations in the **monsoon** and unseasonal rains in **2024** led to volatility in **food inflation**, particularly affecting the prices of vegetables and cereals.
 
 
 
• **Heatwaves of 2024**:
 
 
• During the **summer of 2024**, parts of **North** and **Central India** recorded temperatures exceeding **50°C**, creating a severe **public health** crisis and increasing the **peak electricity demand** to record levels.
 
 
 
• **Climate Risk Index**:
 
 
• The ranking of India as the **seventh** most vulnerable country aligns with findings from the **Global Climate Risk Index**, which assesses the extent to which countries have been affected by the impacts of weather-related loss events.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives**:
 
 
• To combat these risks, India has accelerated its **National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)** and emphasized the **National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change (NAFCC)**.
 
• India remains committed to its **Panchamrit** targets announced at **COP26**, aiming for **Net Zero** emissions by the year **2070**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Economic Survey 2024-25**: This document is prepared by the **Economics Division** of the **Department of Economic Affairs** under the guidance of the **Chief Economic Advisor (CEA)**.
 
• **Macro-Critical Risk**: The survey categorizes climate change as a **macro-critical risk**, meaning it has the potential to affect the **GDP growth**, **fiscal deficit**, and **financial stability** of the country.
 
• **Disaster Management**: The increasing frequency of events on **93%** of days necessitates a shift from **reactive relief** to **proactive disaster resilient infrastructure**, as promoted by the **CDRI (Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure)**.
 
• **Mission LiFE**: Launched by the **Prime Minister**, this mission encourages an environmentally conscious lifestyle to mitigate the long-term effects of global warming at an individual and community level.

questions.question: Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award 2024 winner, D Gukesh, is associated with which sports?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chess**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dommaraju Gukesh**, popularly known as **D Gukesh**, is a prominent Indian **Grandmaster** in the sport of **Chess**.
 
• He has been selected for the **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award 2024**, which is the highest sporting honor in **India**, following his historic achievements on the global stage.
 
• In **April 2024**, **D Gukesh** made history by becoming the **youngest-ever challenger** for the **World Chess Championship** title after winning the **FIDE Candidates Tournament** in **Toronto**, **Canada**, at the age of **17**.
 
• He played a crucial role in leading the **Indian Men’s Team** to their first-ever **Gold Medal** at the **45th FIDE Chess Olympiad** held in **Budapest**, **Hungary**, in **September 2024**.
 
• He achieved an individual **Gold Medal** on the **first board** during the **Olympiad**, finishing with a phenomenal performance rating of over **3000**.
 
• **Gukesh** is currently the **highest-rated Indian chess player**, having surpassed the legendary **Viswanathan Anand** in the **FIDE Live Ratings**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award:**
 
 
• It is awarded annually by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**, Government of India.
 
• The award was formerly known as the **Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award** before being renamed in **August 2021** in honor of the **Hockey** legend **Major Dhyan Chand**.
 
• The first recipient of this prestigious award was the **Chess** legend **Viswanathan Anand** in the year **1991-92**.
 
• The award consists of a **medallion**, a **certificate**, and a significant cash prize of **Rs. 25 lakh**.
 
 
 
• **FIDE (International Chess Federation):**
 
 
• It is the international governing body for the sport of **Chess**, founded on **July 20, 1924**, in **Paris**, **France**.
 
• It organizes the **World Chess Championship** and sets the **Elo rating** system to rank players globally.
 
 
 
• **Grandmaster (GM) Title:**
 
 
• This is the highest title a chess player can attain, awarded by **FIDE**. 
 
• **D Gukesh** became the **second-youngest Grandmaster** in history in **January 2019**, at the age of **12 years, 7 months, and 17 days**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **National Sports Day:** Celebrated in **India** on **August 29** to mark the birth anniversary of **Major Dhyan Chand**. The **National Sports Awards** are typically presented by the **President of India** at **Rashtrapati Bhavan**.
 
• **2024 Context:** The year **2024** has been a landmark year for **Indian Chess**, with both the Men's and Women's teams winning **Olympiad Gold**, making **D Gukesh** a primary candidate for the nation's top honors.
 
• **World Championship 2024:** **D Gukesh** faces the reigning World Champion **Ding Liren** from **China** in the **World Chess Championship** match scheduled for late **2024** in **Singapore**.

questions.question: In May 2025, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) penalised the Union Bank of India and which of the following companies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Transactree Technologies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **May 2025**, the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** exercised its regulatory authority to impose **monetary penalties** on **Union Bank of India** and **Transactree Technologies Private Limited** for various compliance failures.
 
• The penalty on **Union Bank of India** was specifically linked to the violation of **RBI** directions concerning **Lending to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) Sector** and the maintenance of the **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)**.
 
• **Transactree Technologies Private Limited**, which operates as a **Non-Banking Financial Company-Peer to Peer (NBFC-P2P)** lending platform (widely known as **Lendbox**), was penalised for non-compliance with the **Peer-to-Peer Lending Platform (Reserve Bank) Directions, 2017**.
 
• These regulatory actions were taken under the provisions of **Section 47A** of the **Banking Regulation Act, 1949**, and relevant sections of the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**.
 
• The **RBI** clarified that these penalties are based on **deficiencies in regulatory compliance** and are not intended to validate any specific transactions between these entities and their customers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Union Bank of India**:
 
 
• It is one of **India's** largest **Public Sector Banks**, headquartered in **Mumbai**.
 
• The bank was established in **1919** and was inaugurated by **Mahatma Gandhi**.
 
• Following the **2020 Amalgamation**, **Andhra Bank** and **Corporation Bank** were merged into **Union Bank of India**, significantly expanding its footprint to over **8,500 branches**.
 
 
 
• **Transactree Technologies (NBFC-P2P)**:
 
 
• **Peer-to-Peer (P2P)** lending is a method of **debt financing** that allows individuals to borrow and lend money without the use of an official **financial institution** as an intermediary.
 
• The **RBI** regulated this sector in **2017** by categorizing such platforms as **Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs)** to ensure transparent operations and **consumer protection**.
 
• **Transactree Technologies** operates **Lendbox**, which is a leading **fintech** player in the **Indian** credit market.
 
 
 
• **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)**:
 
 
• It is the minimum percentage of **deposits** that a **commercial bank** has to maintain in the form of **liquid cash**, **gold**, or **unencumbered securities**.
 
• It is a key **monetary policy** tool used by the **RBI** to control the **expansion of bank credit** and ensure the **solvency** of banks.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**:
 
 
• The **RBI** was established on **April 1, 1935**, in accordance with the provisions of the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**.
 
• It performs the function of the **Monetary Authority**, the **Regulator and Supervisor of the financial system**, and the **Manager of Foreign Exchange**.
 
• Under the **Banking Regulation Act, 1949**, the **RBI** has the power to inspect **banking companies** and impose fines to maintain **financial stability** in the **Indian economy**.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Oversight**:
 
 
• The **RBI** frequently issues **Master Directions** on **Know Your Customer (KYC)**, **Cyber Security Framework**, and **Interest Rate on Deposits** to protect the interests of depositors.
 
• Failure to adhere to these **norms** results in **enforcement actions**, which serve as a deterrent for other **financial institutions** and **fintech companies**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which prestigious award was Dr. Anandharamakrishnan awarded in 2024 for his contributions to Agricultural Sciences?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vigyan Shri Award**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dr. C. Anandharamakrishnan**, the Director of **CSIR-National Institute for Interdisciplinary Science and Technology (NIIST)**, was honored with the **Vigyan Shri Award** in **2024**.
 
• This award was specifically granted for his pioneering contributions to the field of **Agricultural Sciences**, particularly in food processing and engineering.
 
• The **Vigyan Shri** is a category under the newly instituted **Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar (RVP)**, which is one of the highest national honors in **India** for science, technology, and innovation.
 
• The awards for the year **2024** were announced on **August 7** and presented by the **President of India** on **August 23**, which coincides with **National Space Day**.
 
• **Dr. Anandharamakrishnan** has been recognized for his extensive research in **3D food printing**, **computational modeling of food processing**, and **nutrient delivery systems**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar (RVP):**
 
 
• Introduced by the **Government of India** in **2024**, these awards replaced previous science-related awards to provide a unified recognition system.
 
• The awards are divided into four categories: **Vigyan Ratna** (for lifetime achievement), **Vigyan Shri** (for distinguished contributions), **Vigyan Yuva-SSB** (for young scientists), and **Vigyan Team** (for collaborative work).
 
• The **2024** awards covered **13 domains**, including **Physics**, **Chemistry**, **Biological Sciences**, **Mathematics**, **Agricultural Sciences**, and **Engineering**.
 
 
 
• **Profile of Dr. Anandharamakrishnan:**
 
 
• Before his tenure at **CSIR-NIIST**, he served as the Director of the **National Institute of Food Technology, Entrepreneurship and Management (NIFTEM)** in **Thanjavur**.
 
• He has authored several books and published over **170 research papers** focused on **Food Engineering** and **Agro-processing**.
 
• His work is instrumental in addressing issues like **malnutrition** and enhancing the **shelf-life** of agricultural produce through scientific intervention.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of the Award:** The **Vigyan Shri** honors scientists of any **age** who have made a distinguished contribution to their respective fields of science and technology.
 
• **Selection Committee:** The recipients are selected by a committee chaired by the **Principal Scientific Adviser** to the **Government of India**, including secretaries of various science departments.
 
• **Other Categories:** In **2024**, while **Dr. Anandharamakrishnan** received the **Vigyan Shri**, the **Vigyan Ratna** (the highest in this series) was awarded to **Professor G. Padmanabhan** for his work in **Biological Sciences**.
 
• **Venue and Location:** The **CSIR-NIIST**, headed by the awardee, is a premier research laboratory located in **Thiruvananthapuram**, **Kerala**, which focuses on **sustainable utilization** of regional resources.
</ul

questions.question: In February 2025, which Indian athlete broke the Asian short-track record in the 5000 m with a time of 12:59.77?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gulveer Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Indian long-distance runner **Gulveer Singh** created history in **February 2025** by breaking the **Asian short-track record** in the **5000 m** event.
 
• He clocked a remarkable time of **12:59.77** at the **BU John Thomas Terrier Classic** held in **Boston, USA**.
 
• With this performance, **Gulveer Singh** became the **first Indian athlete** to breach the **13-minute barrier** in the **5000 m** discipline (indoor/short track).
 
• The previous **Asian indoor record** was **13:09.43**, which was set by **El Hassan El-Abbassi** of **Bahrain** in **2012**.
 
• **Gulveer Singh** finished **second** in the race, finishing just behind **Yared Nuguse** of the **USA**, who won the event with a time of **12:56.46**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gulveer Singh:**

 
 
• Hailing from **Sirsa, Uttar Pradesh**, he is a prominent figure in India's middle and long-distance running circuit.
 
• In **March 2024**, he set the **national record** in the **10,000 m** (outdoor) with a time of **27:41.81** at **The TEN** meet in **California**.
 
• He won the **bronze medal** in the **10,000 m** at the **2022 Asian Games** held in **Hangzhou, China**.
 
 
 
• **Avinash Sable:**
 
 
• He is another legendary Indian runner who holds the **outdoor national record** for the **5000 m** (**13:19.30**) and the **3000 m Steeplechase**.
 
• While **Gulveer Singh** broke the short-track record, **Avinash Sable** remains a dominant force in outdoor athletics and **Commonwealth Games** medalists.
 
 
 
• **Short-Track vs. Outdoor Records:**
 
 
• **Short-track** records (often referred to as **indoor** records) are maintained separately from **outdoor** records by **World Athletics**.
 
• Short-track races typically take place on a **200-meter oval**, whereas outdoor tracks are **400 meters** in length.
 
 
 
• **Other Options:**
 
 
• **Jacob Kiplimo** is a world-renowned long-distance runner from **Uganda** and a **World Half Marathon** record holder.
 
• **Yared Nuguse** is an **American** middle-distance runner who competed in the same race in **Boston** where **Gulveer Singh** set the record.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Training and Support:** **Gulveer Singh** trains under the guidance of coach **Scott Simmons** and is supported by the **JSW Sports** program and the **Athletics Federation of India (AFI)**.
 
• **Historical Context:** Entering the sub-13 minute club is considered a world-class milestone in long-distance running, placing **Gulveer Singh** among the elite athletes globally.
 
• **Year of Achievement:** This record was established on **February 1, 2025**, marking a significant start to the athletic season for **India**.
 
• **Venue:** The **Boston University (BU)** track is famous for being a "fast track," frequently producing record-breaking times due to its banking and surface quality.

questions.question: Which of the following countries hosted the 2025 FIFA U-17 World Cup under the new 48-team format?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Qatar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **FIFA Council** officially announced in **March 2024** that **Qatar** will host the next five editions of the **FIFA U-17 World Cup** starting from **2025** to **2029**.
 
• Starting with the **2025** edition, the **FIFA U-17 World Cup** will undergo a massive expansion, increasing the number of participating teams from **24** to **48**.
 
• The tournament, which was previously held every **two years** (biennially), will now be held **annually** to provide more competitive opportunities for young footballers globally.
 
• The decision to grant hosting rights to a single nation for **five consecutive years** was made to ensure stability and efficiency in tournament organization using existing **world-class infrastructure**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Qatar.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup:**
 
 
• Similar to the men's tournament, the **FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup** will also become an **annual** event starting from **2025**.
 
• **Morocco** has been selected as the host for the **five editions** of the women’s tournament from **2025 to 2029**.
 
• The field for the women's tournament will expand to **24 teams**, reflecting **FIFA’s** commitment to growing women's football at the grassroots level.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The **FIFA U-17 World Cup** was first held in **1985** in **China**, where it was originally an **Under-16** event before changing to **Under-17** in **1991**.
 
• **Nigeria** is currently the most successful nation in the history of the men's tournament, having won a record **five titles**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Infrastructure and Legacy:**
 
 
• **Qatar** was chosen largely due to its existing state-of-the-art stadiums and facilities built for the **2022 FIFA World Cup**, which ensures **operational efficiency** and **sustainability**.
 
• This **48-team format** mimics the expansion of the **senior FIFA World Cup**, which will also feature **48 teams** starting in **2026**.
 
 
 
• **Global Development:**

questions.question: In 2025, 36 people including government employees were arrested under “Operation Spot Trap” by the Vigilance and Anti‑Corruption Bureau (VACB). Which state was this operation conducted in?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Operation Spot Trap** was a massive state-wide anti-corruption drive conducted in **January 2025** to weed out bribery and financial irregularities in public offices.
 
• The operation was orchestrated by the **Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB)** of **Kerala**, following numerous complaints regarding "speed money" or illegal commissions being demanded for public services.
 
• A total of **36 people**, including several **government employees** and private **middlemen**, were arrested during the coordinated raids across multiple districts. ***Hence, the statement regarding the location being Kerala is correct.***
 
• The raids primarily targeted departments with high public interaction, such as the **Revenue Department**, **Motor Vehicles Department (MVD)**, and **Local Self-Government (LSG)** institutions.
 
• During the operation, the **VACB** officials seized significant amounts of **unaccounted cash** from the possession of officials and from various hidden spots within government premises.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB):**
 
 
• The **VACB** is the premier agency in **Kerala** dedicated to investigating corruption among public servants. It operates under the **Home Department** of the Government of **Kerala**.
 
• The agency is headed by a Director of the rank of **Director General of Police (DGP)** or **Additional Director General of Police (ADGP)**.
 
• Its primary function is to conduct "trap" operations, surprise checks, and detailed enquiries into assets disproportionate to the known sources of income of **government employees**.
 
 
 
• **Mechanism of Trap Operations:**
 
 
• A "trap" typically involves the use of **phenolphthalein-coated currency notes**. When a public servant accepts this money, their hands are dipped in a sodium carbonate solution, which turns pink, providing scientific evidence of the bribe-taking act.
 
• **Operation Spot Trap** utilized these methods along with advanced surveillance to catch offenders red-handed in **2025**.
 
 
 
• **Legal Framework:**
 
 
• The arrests and subsequent prosecutions are carried out under the **Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988**. This **Act** was significantly amended in **2018** to include provisions for punishing both the bribe-taker and the bribe-giver.
 
• The **VACB** also relies on the **Kerala Government Servants' Conduct Rules** to initiate departmental actions alongside criminal proceedings.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Public Participation:**
 
 
• The **Kerala** government has encouraged citizens to report corruption via the **'Vigilance Eye'** mobile application and a **24/7 toll-free helpline number (1064)**.
 
• This digital integration played a crucial role in gathering the intelligence that led to the success of **Operation Spot Trap** in **January 2025**.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Administration:**
 
 
• Such operations are intended to improve **Kerala's** ranking in the **India Corruption Survey**. Despite being noted as one of the least corrupt states in **India**, the government continues these high-intensity drives to ensure **zero tolerance** for corruption.
 
• The **36 arrests** made in **2025** serve as a deterrent to other officials and emphasize the accountability of the **bureaucracy**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: What is its primary objective of the GoIStats app, launched by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) in 2025?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To give a snapshot of key socio-economic data of the Ministry**__.

• The **GoIStats** mobile application was launched by the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)** in **2025** to revolutionize how official statistics are accessed in India.
 
• The primary objective of this application is to provide a **real-time snapshot** of the country's **key socio-economic indicators**, making high-level data available at the fingertips of users. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• It serves as a **centralized digital platform** where users can find authenticated data regarding **National Income**, **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**, and **Consumer Price Index (CPI)**.
 
• The app is specifically designed to enhance **transparency** and **data accessibility** for researchers, policymakers, students, and the general public, moving away from bulky physical reports to a **digital-first approach**.
 
• By integrating various datasets, the **GoIStats** app helps in monitoring the **economic health** of the nation through interactive visualizations and simplified **statistical dashboards**.

__
 
• **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI):**
 
 
• **MoSPI** came into existence as an independent Ministry on **15th October 1999** after the merger of the Department of Statistics and the Department of Programme Implementation.
 
• The Ministry has two wings: one relating to **Statistics** (National Statistical Office - **NSO**) and the other relating to **Programme Implementation**.

• **Data Reliability:** The data provided on the **GoIStats** app is sourced directly from the **National Statistical Office (NSO)**, ensuring **100% authenticity** and eliminating the risks associated with misinformation.
 
• **User Interface:** The app features **multilingual support** and **offline access** to certain key indicators, ensuring that **data literacy** reaches even the remote corners of the **country**.
 
• **Global Comparison:** The app often provides benchmarks against **Sustainable Development Goals (SDG)**, allowing users to see India's progress on **international indices**.
</ul
